newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian cotton chief plays down smuggling claims.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian cotton chief plays down smuggling claims.

text.p: Smuggling of Tanzanian cotton lint across Lake Victoria to Kenya is a small localised problem and does not affect hard currency earnings, a senior industry official said on Wednesday.
Reacting to local media claims, Tanzania Cotton Seed and Lint Board General Manager Ali Ngongolo told Reuters he did not regard cotton smuggling as a big problem.
"No, it's not a big issue as far as the board is concerned," Ngongolo said. "It's a small localised problem."
The weekly Financial Times newspaper has said that 20 tonnes of cotton lint is being smuggled each week across Lake Victoria into Kenya.
Ngongolo said, "Cotton is bulky. If you take it across the lake to Kenya and gin it, your operation becomes very expensive."
The Financial Times said cotton lint fetched 170 shillings in Tanzania, but could be sold for almost double that in Kenya.
The newspaper report said boats were carrying an average of 200 bales into Kenya, returning with manufactured goods.

Cotton is Tanzania's second biggest agricultural export earner, although prolonged drought around the main cotton growing belt surrounding Lake Victoria is likely to reduce earnings for the 1996/97 crop to just $83 million.
In 1995/96 Tanzania's production totalled 430,000 bales worth an estimated $109 million, compared to 440,000 bales worth $115 million in 1994/95.
One bale is the equivalent of 181 kg.
